mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes CLA 45 AMG engine replacement cost in the UK?

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLA 45 AMG engine reliable? What problems should I watch for?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CLA 45 AMG's M133 and M139 engines are high-performance units with known weak points. The M133 (2013-2019) suffers from turbocharger bearing failure and timing chain tensioner issues. The M139 (2019+) has reported cylinder head valve spring failures and oil consumption. M133 turbocharger failure due to oil feed line contamination - a service campaign was issued. M133 timing chain rattling on cold start signals imminent tensioner failure. M139 broken valve springs causing misfires, rough running and starting problems. M139 oil consumption requiring more frequent top-ups. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for engine longevity. Warning: M139 cylinder head failure can occur at 20,000-50,000 miles - many owners report issues outside warranty.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLA 45 AMG engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the M133 engine can reach 100,000-150,000 miles. The M139 is too new for full longevity data but has reported cylinder head failures at 20,000-50,000 miles in some cases. M133 (2013-2019): 100k-150k miles with regular servicing. M139 (2019+): cylinder head failures reported at 20k-50k miles; well-maintained units may exceed 100k miles. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles (not Mercedes' 15,000-18,000 mile interval) significantly extends life.

mainEntity.name: Which Mercedes CLA 45 AMG engine should I avoid when buying used?

acceptedAnswer.text: All CLA 45 AMG models use high-performance engines, but the M133 (2013-2019) has well-documented turbocharger and timing chain issues. The M139 (2019+) has cylinder head and oil consumption concerns. 2013-2015 M133: turbocharger failure and timing chain tensioner issues. 2016-2019 M133: improved but turbo failures still reported. 2019-2021 M139: cylinder head valve spring failures reported. 2022+ M139: improved but monitor for oil consumption. Always check service history for regular oil changes using Mercedes-approved oil.

mainEntity.name: How much does turbocharger replacement cost on a Mercedes CLA 45 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Turbocharger replacement on a CLA 45 AMG M133 engine costs £2,800-£3,800 at a specialist or £4,000-£5,500 at a main dealer. If turbo debris has circulated through the engine, full engine replacement at £5,500-£8,000 is required. Specialist turbocharger replacement: £2,800-£3,800 including parts and labour. Dealer pricing for same work: £4,000-£5,500. AMG issued a service campaign for turbo failure due to oil feed line contamination. If turbo debris has contaminated the oil system, full engine replacement is required.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Mercedes CLA 45 AMG?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A CLA 45 AMG is worth £15,000-£50,000 depending on generation - a rebuilt engine at £5,500-£11,000 represents roughly 15-30% of the car's value, making replacement economically justifiable for a car in otherwise good condition. CLA 45 AMG with good body/interior: replacement engine is cost-effective. Specialist rebuilt engines fix original design weaknesses and include warranty. Compare against £7,000-£12,000 main dealer new engine quotes.

mainEntity.name: Mercedes CLA 45 AMG vs CLA 35 AMG - is the engine the same?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The CLA 45 AMG uses the M133 (first-generation) or M139 (second-generation) engine with significantly higher power output (360-421 hp), while the CLA 35 AMG uses the M260 DE20 LA engine (306 hp). They are not interchangeable. CLA 45 AMG (2013-2019): M133, 360-381 hp. CLA 45 / 45 S AMG (2019+): M139, 387-421 hp - hand-built AMG engine. CLA 35 AMG (2019+): M260 DE20 LA, 306 hp - different engine family. Engine codes, mounting points and electronics are not compatible between the two.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLA 45 AMG - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes-AMG CLA 45 debuted in 2013 as the flagship performance variant of the CLA range, powered by the M133 2.0-litre turbocharged four-cylinder - at the time the world's most powerful production four-cylinder engine. For the second-generation C118 from 2019, the CLA 45 received the hand-built M139 engine, delivering up to 421 hp and cementing the CLA 45 S as one of the most potent compact performance cars on the market.

milestones.description: M133 DE20 LA, 2.0L turbo petrol, 360 hp, 450 Nm - C117 CLA 45 AMG launch; world's most powerful production four-cylinder at launch
M133 DE20 LA (facelift), 2.0L turbo petrol, 381 hp, 475 Nm - C117 facelift; power increase to 381 hp
M139 DE20 LA, 2.0L turbo petrol, 387 hp (CLA 45) / 421 hp (CLA 45 S) - C118 second-generation launch; hand-built AMG engine; 8-speed DCT
CLA 45 S 4MATIC+ debuts with 421 hp, 500 Nm; 0-62 mph in 4.0 seconds
CLA 45 S continues with M139 DE20 LA; 48V mild hybrid on some markets

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLA 45 AMG Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes-AMG CLA 45 is powered by two generations of hand-built 2.0-litre turbocharged engines - the M133 (2013-2019) and the M139 (2019-present). Both are high-performance units that demand specialist knowledge for repair and replacement. The M133 is known for turbocharger bearing failure and timing chain tensioner issues, while the M139 has reported cylinder head valve spring failures and oil consumption. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Turbocharger Bearing Failure - Why the M133 Engine Fails Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The high-boost turbocharger (up to 2.0 bar) places extreme stress on journal bearings. Oil starvation or contamination accelerates wear, leading to shaft play, compressor wheel contact with the housing, and eventual turbo seizure. AMG initiated a service campaign for turbocharger failure due to contamination of the oil feed line . The M133 engine's lack of a bypass valve can also lead to compressor surge and accelerated turbo damage .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove and replace turbocharger with OEM-spec unit, new oil feed lines, fresh oil and filter
repairOptions.longevity: 50,000-80,000 miles; valid if bottom end and top end are healthy

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt M133 engine with upgraded turbo bearings, new oil pump, and recalibrated wastegate
repairOptions.longevity: 80,000+ miles; recommended when turbo debris has circulated through the engine

problems.recommendation: On a CLA 45 AMG, we rarely recommend turbo-only replacement unless the failure was caught immediately. Turbo debris almost always contaminates the oil system, and the cost of a second failure justifies going straight to a fully rebuilt engine with upgraded turbo components. At £5,500-£8,000 from a specialist, it's expensive - but it's half what Mercedes main dealers charge for a new engine.

problems.h4: Cylinder Head & Valve Spring Failure - M139 Engine Misfires and Rough Running
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes CLA 45 AMG / CLA 45 S (M139 DE20 LA, 2019-present)
problems.rootCause: Broken valve springs in the cylinder head have been reported on M139 engines, particularly in 2020 models . This typically manifests as a Check Engine Light (CEL), rough engine operation, difficulty starting, or ECO stop/start malfunctions . Some owners have reported cylinder head replacement as a 19-hour job costing approximately $10,000 . Misfires on individual cylinders have also been reported .

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cylinder head with updated components, new valve springs, gaskets and bolts
Supply & fit fully rebuilt M139 engine with upgraded cylinder head components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: 50,000+ miles or when cylinder head failure has caused bottom-end damage

problems.recommendation: Cylinder head failure is a significant issue affecting the M139 engine. If you experience misfires, loss of power, or engine management lights, get a compression test and cylinder head inspection immediately. If caught early, cylinder head replacement at £4,500-£6,500 from a specialist resolves the issue. However, if the failure has been ignored and bottom-end damage has occurred, full rebuilt engine replacement at £7,000-£11,000 is the only safe option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M139 DE20 LA Mercedes CLA 45 AMG engine prices

problems.h4: Oil Consumption - High-Performance AMG Engine Oil Burning
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes CLA 45 AMG (M133 DE20 LA, M139 DE20 LA, 2013-present)
problems.rootCause: High-performance engines with forced induction can experience oil consumption due to piston ring wear, turbocharger oil seal failure, or PCV system issues. M139 engines have been reported to require more frequent oil top-ups between services . M133 engines can suffer from oil leaks from the valve cover gasket and oil filter housing . Aggressive driving and infrequent oil changes accelerate wear.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve cover gasket, oil filter housing gasket, PCV valve
repairOptions.longevity: Effective for external leaks; does not address internal consumption

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full engine strip, replace piston rings, hone cylinders, new gaskets and bolts
repairOptions.longevity: 40,000-70,000 miles; labour-intensive but retains original engine block

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit fully rebuilt engine with upgraded piston rings, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: 70,000+ miles or when oil consumption exceeds 1L/1,000 miles

problems.recommendation: On a CLA 45 AMG burning oil excessively, we typically recommend full rebuilt engine replacement rather than just piston rings. The labour to strip and rebuild is almost identical, but a factory-rebuilt unit includes all new bearings, seals, and timing components - and the upgraded rings that fix the design weakness. The price difference is often just £1,000-£2,000, and the rebuilt engine comes with a 12-month warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Rattling on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to slacken and produce a rattling or ticking noise on startup . If ignored, the timing chain can jump teeth, causing valves and pistons to collide . Cases of premature chain stretching have been reported, especially with infrequent oil changes or aggressive operation . The M133 engine shares this weakness with the wider M270 engine family.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; tensioner replacement only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets
Supply & fit fully rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components, bench tested, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has slipped and valves have contacted pistons

problems.recommendation: Rattling on cold start for 1-2 seconds is the early warning sign of timing chain tensioner failure. Don't ignore it - specialist tensioner replacement at £700-£1,100 or full timing chain replacement at £1,800-£2,500 resolves the issue if done promptly. If you've been driving with the rattle for months, the chain has almost certainly stretched, and we'd advise moving straight to a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components.
